sky.content: Sunlight appears white but is actually composed of a spectrum of colors, each with a different wavelength. As this light enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with air molecules, causing shorter blue wavelengths to scatter in all directions much more efficiently than longer red wavelengths. This scattered blue light reaches our eyes from every part of the sky, making it appear blue during the day.
